cases.name: Shurtleff v. Boston

components.issue: Religious viewpoint in a public flag program
components.decision: Held that Boston’s exclusion of the religious flag violated free speech.
components.scope: The program facilitated private expression; the Court did not require government itself to endorse a religious message.
components.survey_fit: The question addresses Boston’s particular exclusion. The outcome corresponds to the violation answer, selected by 44.3%.

cases.interpretation_limit: All nine justices agreed in the judgment, but the survey point estimate favored the other answer. Votes are not policy magnitude. Polling ended before the ruling; the report was published afterward.

cases.name: Carson v. Makin

components.issue: Religious schools in an existing tuition program
components.decision: Invalidated Maine’s exclusion of religious schools from otherwise available tuition assistance.
components.scope: Access to the existing program, not a requirement to establish private-school subsidies in every state.
components.survey_fit: The poll describes the Maine funding exclusion. The Court’s result corresponds to the violation answer, selected by 48.7%.

cases.interpretation_limit: The 48.7% versus 51.3% division is close; no statistically established disagreement or Court-wide alignment rate is inferred.
